universalAnswers.whatHappened: Nature Medicine posted an accepted-article preview reporting CRISP’s comparison results on frozen-section pathology images during surgery.
universalAnswers.plainLanguageIdentity: Frozen sections give a pathologist a rapid tissue image while surgery continues; CRISP supplies a prediction for the pathologist to interpret.
universalAnswers.evidenceBasis: The accepted paper reports prospective observational comparisons with other models and a reader study including pathologists.
universalAnswers.evidenceLimits: The paper says a prospective interventional study is still needed to assess deployment and clinical outcomes.
universalAnswers.readerRelevance: The story shows why an AI comparison result in a difficult clinical task can be meaningful without being proof of better care.
universalAnswers.affectedPeople: The study involved adult surgical patients and pathology teams at three prospective-study centres; no personal care recommendation follows.
universalAnswers.changesNow: The accepted-article preview reports research; it does not establish routine clinical availability.
universalAnswers.uncertainty: The authors require prospective interventional study, more diverse validation and work on regulation, workflow integration and training.
universalAnswers.readerAction: Read the study as evidence about model and workflow performance under its stated conditions, not as medical advice or proof of better outcomes.
universalAnswers.betterQuestion: Did the study measure prediction performance, workflow support or an actual improvement in patient outcomes?

health-science.aiRole: CRISP divides slide images into patches, extracts numerical features, weights salient regions and produces slide-level predictions.
health-science.professionalRole: A pathologist remains responsible for interpreting the tissue and informing the surgical team; the article describes CRISP as support.
health-science.evidenceLevel: Accepted peer-reviewed research with retrospective tasks, a prospective observational study and a separate simulated deployment analysis; not an interventional trial or approval.
health-science.benefitClaim: The article reports prediction and workflow measures. This candidate makes no treatment or patient-outcome benefit claim.
health-science.risksAndFalseResults: The paper reports false positives associated mainly with rare benign tumours and false negatives mainly with rare malignant tumours with ambiguous morphology.
health-science.availability: The paper does not establish routine clinical availability, local access or regulatory authorization.
health-science.readerBoundary: This research explanation is not medical advice and is not a reason to change personal care.

research-benchmark.researchQuestion: Can a frozen-section-specific imaging model support diagnostic and predictive tasks in intraoperative pathology?
research-benchmark.method: Development used 103,797 slides obtained primarily from ten centres; prospective observational evaluation enrolled 3,064 patients at three centres, including 2,071 at SYCC, with a separate 100-case simulation.
research-benchmark.result: The study measured model predictions and workflow-related analyses; the candidate does not turn those into a clinical-impact claim.
research-benchmark.sponsorAndInterests: The paper authors performed and reported the work; the candidate relies on the peer-reviewed accepted paper and journal record.
research-benchmark.independentReplication: No independent replication was verified for this candidate.
research-benchmark.realWorldTransfer: Prospective observation tests performance under real workflows, while the separate deployment/timing analysis was simulated. Neither proves better patient outcomes.
research-benchmark.limitations: Retrospective registration, no prospective intervention, population diversity, regulatory compliance, workflow integration and user training remain limits.

translation.newsVersionExact: Most existing AI learned from usual preserved slides, whose look differs from frozen tissue. CRISP was trained for frozen images. In an observational study — researchers watched normal care — it beat other AI models.
translation.actualMeaningExact: Frozen images must be read quickly.
translation.mechanismExact: CRISP gives a prediction; the pathologist still interprets the tissue.
translation.familiarExampleExact: During surgery, a pathologist — a specialist who examines tissue to identify disease — may need an answer before the next step.

jargon.plainMeaning: A frozen section is tissue quickly frozen, sliced and examined during surgery.

learningConnections.concept: A measured result is bounded by its task and conditions.
learningConnections.learningPayoff: AI Fundamentals 101 chapter 12.3 explains why a test does not establish readiness for a different real-world job.
